correctness.rationale: For arbitrary strictly positive legs, each simplex is coordinatewise between its first and last vertices, giving a Minkowski-sum bounding box with both opposite corners attained. Coordinatewise Euclidean differences give the exact diameter, and the pointwise squared-distance identity gives the unique midpoint minimum ball; sphere equality forces every nonconstant coordinate to be a box endpoint. A factor attaining such an endpoint has normalized binary monotone coordinates and thus is a single step vertex. Overlap chains force one binary step per component union, giving the exact product of (length+1) contacts. A step whose complement is also a step must be constant on that component, giving 2^(c−1) unordered diameter pairs. The binomial specialization follows by Vandermonde and subtraction of k=0,1 terms. The included standard-library exact checker independently enumerates 1,245 finite parameter instances and passes 11,278 assertions; the proof does not extrapolate from these finite cases.

value.rationale: The recently studied all-rank Kozlov Minkowski sums have incomplete general vertex structure; a complete extremal metric classification without enumerating all vertices is a natural and useful structural invariant. The theorem supplies all sphere contacts, every diametral pair, a binomial autocorrelation diameter for Kozlov legs, and an exact change at the shift-overlap threshold. It is not merely the standard box-radius inequality: the nontrivial componentwise corner-realizability and count, with sharp multiplicities and all ranks, are the substantive content.
